title: Closed models [notes postérieures à PS ?] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page has three small commutative squares drawn on recycled scrap paper: an IBM JCL listing for an assembler/linkage-editor job, printed sideways and unrelated to the mathematics. They are the elementary lifting configurations Grothendieck is using while trying to prove Quillen's 'covering homotopy extension theorem' (Homotopical Algebra, Ch. II §2.4, Prop. 4), which was set up on p.20 and is continued on p.22.

(1) Square A --α--> X, A --> A×I on the left (labelled roughly 'cof.' or 'ac.'), X --p--> Y on the right, A×I --h--> Y along the bottom, with a diagonal A×I --> X. This is the covering homotopy property. A homotopy h of pα lifts to a homotopy of α because A --> A×I (inclusion at an end) is a trivial cofibration and p is a fibration.

(2) The dual square. Top: X --> A. Bottom: Y --> A^I. Right: Y --> X, labelled 'cofib.'. Left: ∂0 : A^I --> A, labelled 'fib.'. This is the homotopy extension property in path-object form. Given a map X --> A and a homotopy on the subobject Y (a map Y --> A^I starting at the restriction), one extends the homotopy to X. The extension is a lift X --> A^I, using that ∂0 is a trivial fibration when A is fibrant.

(3) A generic lifting square A --> X, A --> B, X --> Y, B --> Y, with a diagonal B --> X. This is the abstract lifting axiom of which (1) and (2) are special cases.

There are also two small doodles of arrows inside ovals, and stray marks ('/', 'Y_x').

The purpose is to recall the lifting properties needed on p.22. There he tries to make the two homotopies φi ~ g and pφ ~ g' compatible, and reduces this to a lifting problem of the trivial cofibration X⊔X --> X⊗I against the fibration p.
errors: For the lifts to exist, the left vertical in (1) must be a trivial cofibration (not merely a cofibration), and ∂0 in (2) must be a trivial fibration (true when A is fibrant). The labels 'cof.' and 'fib.' omit 'trivial', unless the scribbled 'af.' or 'ac.' means acyclic. This is notational shorthand, not a real error.

ideas.what: Covering homotopy property: lifting a homotopy along a fibration, via lifting of A --> A×I against p
ideas.modern_name: homotopy lifting property / right lifting property of fibrations against trivial cofibrations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hurewicz, Serre (classical); Quillen 1967 for the model-category form
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks discusses fibrations and lifting in this general style; exact diagram unsure

ideas.what: Homotopy extension property via the path object, ∂0 : A^I --> A against a cofibration

ideas.modern_name: lifting axiom of a closed model category
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks (uses model-category lifting axioms throughout)

deep.surprise_reason: These are textbook lifting diagrams jotted on scrap paper as an aid to the argument on the neighbouring pages. No new result or connection appears.
transcription_corrections: The left vertical arrow of the first square is labelled something like 'af.' or 'ac.' (possibly 'acyclic'), not clearly 'cof.'; its top arrow is α, bottom h, right p, and there is a drawn diagonal arrow A×I --> X.

In the second square the arrows point up and left. ∂0 : A^I --> A is labelled 'fib' (with crossed-out scribbles); the right arrow Y --> X is labelled 'cofib.'; the horizontal arrows are X --> A and Y --> A^I.
In the third square the bottom-left object is B (written like 'ß'), and a diagonal arrow B --> X is drawn.
'λ' is more likely a stray slash '/'.
'Y_x' is a stray mark of uncertain meaning.
The typescript is an IBM JCL listing ('//PREDONTA JOB CNU0049-PREDONT,...'), confirmed to be unrelated scrap.
